findings.title: FR-5(d) unreceipted-signal gauge has zero production callers and is not in the invariant gauge registry
findings.evidence: countUnreceiptedOverdue (lib/fleet/outstanding-signals.cjs:217, exported line 276) is referenced ONLY by its own definition, its own comment, and tests/unit/fleet/count-unreceipted-overdue.test.js. Repo-wide grep across .js/.cjs/.mjs finds no production caller. It is also absent from lib/governance/gauge-registry.js, the canonical Invariant Gauges Registry (SD-LEO-INFRA-INVARIANT-GAUGES-FRAMEWORK-001) holding ~25 named live gauges. AC-15 as literally worded is fully met (0 with receipts, N without, unknown on throw - all three asserted). But FR-5(d) states its purpose as 'asserted at zero from the merge commit' per ratification 49656c8c's preventive-exit-predicate requirement, and that is NOT operational: a pure function nobody invokes cannot assert anything against live data. Contrast with the other two mechanisms, which ARE wired: capped-pool-broadcast tick() is called at scripts/stale-session-sweep.cjs:4424-4441, and stampConstraintsBlock at lib/coordinator/dispatch.cjs:1488 with a structural wiring test. This is the zero-yield / dead-by-construction-while-reading-as-wired pattern. RECOMMENDATION: either register the gauge in lib/governance/gauge-registry.js (or call it from a coordinator health surface), or amend the PRD to record FR-5(d) as forward-capacity rather than a live exit predicate. Not a FAIL because every enumerated AC passes; the gap is between AC-15 and FR-5(d)'s prose.
